CNP Rights
RBAC with Object-Level Overrides
This model uses Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) as the primary mechanism with two
override layers for the cases where standard roles aren't enough.
Hierarchy
Every configuration value resolves through a three-layer hierarchy. The engine always returns
the most specific value available, falling back up the chain if no override exists at a lower level.
The permission resolution algorithm always returns the most specific applicable permission.
Layer 3 overrides Layer 2 overrides Layer 1. An explicit Revoke at any layer beats a Grant at a
lower layer. Cannot work around a revocation by granting at a lower layer.
State-specific additions or removals from the base role. Utah grants StateReviewer access to
DirectVer. Maine removes the auto-approve permission 
Lives in cnp_ops
if user level override exists, it moves to layer 3 →
Individual user grants or revocations. Temporary access for a contractor. Restricted access for a
user under investigation. 
Requires justification + expiry date
Lives in cnp_ops. 
The base set of permissions every role has by default across all states. StateReviewer always
includes SNP.Applications.Approve.
Lives in cnp_global
Example: LateClaimCutoffDays = 6
if tenant override exists, it moves to layer 2→
Layer 1 — Role Permissions 
Layer 2 — Tenant Role Overrides
Layer 3 — User Permission Overrides 
IsFederal blocks revocation at all layers

Permission Catalog Structure
Actions vocabulary
Reports are governed by domain access. A user with SNP.Claims.View  can view SNP claim
reports. A user with SNP.Claims.Export  can export them. Report-specific gates (e.g., FNS-
10 is Finance-only) are handled by the Accounting.FNSReports.Export  permission. This
collapses the existing report permission sprawl into the domain model.
The PermissionCatalog has approximately 180 entries: 8 domains × ~4 sub-areas × ~5 actions,
plus some domain-specific extras. The state-specific variation is handled by
TenantRoleOverrides, not by individual permission entries.
How Permissions Resolve at Runtime
The service is cached per-request so it doesn't re-query the database on every permission
check within a single request. The cache is invalidated when a UserRoleAssignment or
TenantRoleOverride is written, and at midnight UTC for any expiring assignments.

1 // ICnpPermissionService — the only interface application code uses for authorization
2 public interface ICnpPermissionService {
3 bool HasPermission(string userId, string tenantCode, string permissionCode);
4 IEnumerable<string> GetPermissions(string userId, string tenantCode);
5 bool HasRole(string userId, string tenantCode, string roleCode);
6 bool HasSponsorAccess(string userId, string tenantCode, int sponsorId);
7 }
8
9 // Resolution algorithm (simplified)
10 bool HasPermission(userId, tenantCode, permissionCode) {
11
12 // 1. Check user-level override first (highest priority)
13 var userOverride = UserPermissionOverrides
14 .Where(o => o.UserId == userId && o.TenantCode == tenantCode
15 && o.PermissionCode == permissionCode
16 && (o.ExpiresAt == null || o.ExpiresAt > NOW()))
17 .FirstOrDefault();
18 if (userOverride?.OverrideType == "Revoke") return false;
19 if (userOverride?.OverrideType == "Grant") return true;
20
21 // 2. Extract domain from permission code (e.g. "SNP" from "SNP.Claims.View")
22 //    and get user's role assignments for this tenant, filtered by DomainScope when set
23 var domain = permissionCode.Split('.')[0];
24
25 var assignments = UserRoleAssignments
26 .Where(r => r.UserId == userId && r.TenantCode == tenantCode
27 && (r.ExpiresAt == null || r.ExpiresAt > NOW())
28 && (r.DomainScope == null || r.DomainScope == domain));
29
30 var systemRoleIds = assignments.Where(a => a.RoleId != null).Select(a => a.RoleId);
31 var tenantRoleIds = assignments.Where(a => a.TenantRoleId != null).Select(a =>
a.TenantRoleId);
32
33 // 3. Check system roles (cnp_global) — TenantRoleOverride and IsFederal logic applies
34 foreach (var roleId in systemRoleIds) {
35 var tenantOverride = TenantRoleOverrides
36 .Where(o => o.RoleId == roleId && o.TenantCode == tenantCode
37 && o.PermissionCode == permissionCode)
38 .FirstOrDefault();
39 if (tenantOverride?.OverrideType == "Revoke") continue;
40 if (tenantOverride?.OverrideType == "Grant") return true;
41
42 // Fall back to base role permission
43 if (RolePermissions.Any(rp => rp.RoleId == roleId && rp.PermissionCode ==
permissionCode))
44 return true;
45 }
46
47 // 4. Check tenant-defined roles (cnp_ops) — permissions are direct, no overrides apply
48 foreach (var tenantRoleId in tenantRoleIds) {
49 if (TenantRolePermissions.Any(rp => rp.TenantRoleId == tenantRoleId
50 && rp.PermissionCode == permissionCode))
51 return true;
52 }
53
54 // 5. No grant found at any layer
55 return false;
56 }

TenantRolePermissions can only reference permissions the tenant's StateAgencyAdmin
system role already has — a tenant-defined role cannot exceed the ceiling of the highest
system role
The OIDC Connection
The OIDC broker handles authentication (who you are). The ICnpPermissionService handles 
authorization (what you can do). These are deliberately separated.
The OIDC token includes the user's role assignments and tenant scopes so the application can
bootstrap the permission service without a database roundtrip on every request. It does not
include the full permission list.
JWT claims payload (relevant fields)
The broker validates, the service resolvesThe OIDC broker validates that the token is
authentic (signature, expiry, issuer). The ICnpPermissionService resolves what permissions
those roles carry for the requested tenant, applying all overrides. Application code calls
ICnpPermissionService. It never parses JWT claims directly for authorization decisions. 
The optional domain  field indicates a domain-scoped assignment. When present, the
permission service only applies that role's permissions when evaluating permissions in the
matching domain. Omitting domain  is equivalent to null — the role applies across all domains.
Sponsor-Scoped Access
The most nuanced part of CNP rights is sponsor-scoped access. A school district director
should be able to view and submit their own district's claims, but not see other districts' claims.
A state agency reviewer should be able to see all sponsors in their state. A LINQ config admin
should be able to see configuration across all states but not operational sponsor data.
The ScopeType  on UserRoleAssignments handles this without requiring object-level ACLs for
every sponsor.

<!-- page: 11 -->
The ICnpPermissionService's HasSponsorAccess(userId, tenantCode, sponsorId)
method encapsulates this check. Application code calls it before returning any sponsor-scoped
data. The query filter is injected automatically at the repository layer for all sponsor-scoped
entities.
A sponsor user's access to their own data is enforced by individual permission rows per object.
In the new model, ScopeType=SpecificSponsor on their role assignment is a single row that
enforces the boundary for every entity type in the system so thereʼs no per-object permission
management required.
Domain-Scoped Access
DomainScope  on UserRoleAssignments is the program-dimension parallel to SponsorId .
Where sponsor scoping answers "which organizations can this user see?", domain scoping
answers "which programs can this user operate in?" States with separate staff for different
nutrition programs assign Caseworker with DomainScope = 'SNP' to one group and
DomainScope = 'CACFP' to another. A second assignment can be added independently if
responsibilities expand. 
IsFederal Guardrails in the Rights Model
The same IsFederal guardrail pattern used in the workflow engine and CnpDefaults applies here.
Certain role-permission combinations are federally required and cannot be revoked by any
tenant or user override.

Migration from Existing CnpObjects
Migrating from 5,082 individual ACL rows to the new RBAC model is a data exercise, not a code
exercise. The architect's domain document gives us the structure we need — the 12 domains
and 67 sub-areas map directly to the PermissionCatalog's Domain + SubArea columns.

IsFederal =! "the user has this permission forever"
IsFederal on a RolePermission means the permission cannot be removed from the role via
an override. A user can still lose the permission by having their role assignment revoked
entirely. 
The distinction: IsFederal protects the role definition; it doesn't protect the user
assignment. A state agency can remove someone from the Reviewer role. They cannot
make the Reviewer role unable to create compliance reviews.

Phase 1 scope: SECURITY domain only
The Phase 1 Security & Configuration module means migrating the SECURITY domain first . This
is the smallest domain and the natural starting point. Once the RBAC model is proven for
SECURITY, CONFIGURATION follows, and then the program domains in Phase 3 order (SNP →
CACFP → SFSP).
DIS/CTS convergence through TenantRoleOverrides DIS states have different access
patterns than CTS states. In the new model these differences become TenantRoleOverrides.
Same engine, same roles, different per-tenant configuration.
